name: ultra.forecasting
description: ULTRA Forecasting studio: is this forecast worth averaging into the swarm? Probabilities themselves come from the swarm and are combined in code (trimmed mean, Brier, weights); nothing here asks Jev to predict.

reason_quality.instructions: How well is this forecast reasoned, judged only on its text
criteria: no reasoning at all, or reasoning that restates the number
assertion plus a generic reason that would fit any outcome
cites a mechanism but not a reference class
names a reference class with its own base rate
reference class, base rate, and the specific considerations for and against this case
as above, plus what would update the number and which is load-bearing

reference_class_named.instructions: This forecast names an explicit reference class (a set of comparable past cases), not just this project.

anchored_on_author.instructions: This number was anchored on the plan author's own prior estimate rather than derived independently.

disagreement_is_factual.instructions: Where this forecast disagrees with the evidence pack, the disagreement rests on a factual claim, not on mood or optimism.

cause_is_testable.instructions: This premortem cause could be confirmed or killed by a cheap probe before we commit.

rules.reason: an unreasoned number must not enter the swarm average
no outside view: this is an inside-view guess (Halawi et al. ablate exactly this)
author-anchored forecast: averaging it in manufactures false agreement
disagreement is vibes-shaped: send it back to Research
untestable premortem cause: it will not produce a tripwire

notes.reason_quality: doc signal f.reason_quality; 6 levels so the mean stays interpretable (max 11 allowed).
notes.anchored_on_author: doc signal f.anchored_on_author; motivates dropping the author's own number from the median.
notes.cause_is_testable: doc signal pm.cause_is_testable; single-token name required by the rule grammar.
